items.stem: Several teams keep rewriting near-identical prompts. What is the most durable fix?

options.text: Create parameterised templates in a shared, tagged library for reuse
options.rationale: Correct: templating with variables removes duplication and aids reuse.

options.text: Ask each team to keep their own private copies
options.rationale: Private copies perpetuate drift and duplication.

options.text: Paste the current prompt into a chat whenever needed
options.rationale: Ad-hoc pasting is not durable or discoverable.

options.text: Use the longest prompt any team has written
options.rationale: Length is not a reuse strategy.

items.explanation: Correct: templating with variables removes duplication and aids reuse.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO governance controls belong on a production prompt library? (Select TWO.)

options.text: An approval workflow before a prompt reaches production
options.rationale: Correct: review before production is a core governance control.

options.text: A named owner and access controls for each shared prompt
options.rationale: Correct: ownership and access control establish accountability.
Open editing removes accountability and review.

options.text: No record of who changed what

items.explanation: Correct: review before production is a core governance control.

items.stem: You are retiring an old prompt version. What should always accompany the change?

options.text: An audit trail recording what changed, why, and the replacement
options.rationale: Correct: a deprecation record preserves traceability and supports rollback.
Silent deletion loses history and accountability.
Abrupt removal can break dependents and erase history.

options.text: Only a note in a private chat
options.rationale: A private note is not an auditable record.

items.explanation: Correct: a deprecation record preserves traceability and supports rollback.
